nodes.line: Give me a second. Right. Go.

I have been putting it off since Easter. The Marayong order has been two cartons light every week since the long weekend and the invoice says otherwise every time. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. They admitted it, which I did not expect, so now there is $98 owing to Marayong and it is not going to walk in here itself. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. That's it. That's the whole ask.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

choices.text: The Credit Note, Marayong — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
You are not from around the corner, are you.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. I do the Marayong run at twenty past four and there is a stretch of it where the van gets followed, which I have told nobody until now. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. If it's nothing, it's nothing. Tell me anyway.

Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. I have got a whiteboard with last March still on it in the back of the van and the Marayong shop is shut, and the number on the door rings out. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. If anyone asks, you were never here.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.
Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Iolanda, the kid on the register at Marayong

nodes.line: Half of this suburb has walked past already. Not one stopped.

I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. Three of the Marayong regulars have started coming in together and going out separately, and the till is $14 down on those days. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.

You will think I am making this up. Everything Marayong sells comes off a floor at Quakers Hill, and the woman who runs it will tell you things she will not put in writing. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. I'll see you right for it.
Well? I can read your face from here.
Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Whatever it is, I have had worse this week.

You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Dragan, bushcare volunteer at Central Chalmers Street

nodes.line: I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

I have been putting it off since Easter. Somebody has been tipping fill into the creek behind Central Chalmers Street since the first of the month and it is narrowing the channel a metre at a time. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. They have agreed to a clean-up at Central Chalmers Street, which is wonderful, except the grant is $95 short and closes on the first of the month. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. That's it. That's the whole ask.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

choices.text: The Creek Behind Central Chalmers Street — that's done.
Willow Removal, Central Chalmers Street — that's done.

npcs.name: Zelda, SES member at Central Chalmers Street

nodes.line: Ah. Someone with two working legs.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. We had 94 sandbags in the Central Chalmers Street shed on the first of the month and this morning we have got the pallet they came on. I have got no proof, which is exactly why I am asking. If it's nothing, it's nothing. Tell me anyway.

Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. People keep driving the low crossing at Central Chalmers Street at half six with the water over the sign, and one of them is going to be the one. It might be nothing. It has not felt like nothing. If anyone asks, you were never here.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

nodes.line: You are early. Or late. I have lost track.

I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. The water came through my place at Central Chalmers Street on the first of the month and the assessor wants photographs of things I have already thrown out. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. There is no rush, but there is a Friday.

You will think I am making this up. Whatever is happening to Central Chalmers Street starts upstream at Museum, and there are people up there who have been saying so for years. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. I'll see you right for it.
I had a feeling. Go on.

Upstream, Central Chalmers Street — that's done.
